{{Short description|Type of category in mathematics}}
In mathematics, especially [[category theory]], a '''Reedy category''' is a category ''R'' that has a structure so that the [[functor category]] from ''R'' to a [[model category]] ''M'' would also get the induced model category structure. A prototypical example is the [[simplex category]] or its opposite. It was introduced by Christopher Reedy in his unpublished manuscript.<ref>Reedy's manuscript can be found at https://math.mit.edu/~psh/</ref>

== Definition ==
A Reedy category consists of the following data: a category ''R'', two [[wide subcategory|wide]] (lluf) subcategories <math>R_-, R_+</math> and a functorial factorization of each map into a map in <math>R_-</math> followed by a map in <math>R_+</math> that are subject to the condition: for some total preordering (degree), the nonidentity maps in <math>R_-, R_+</math> lower or raise degrees.<ref>{{harvnb|Barwick|2007|loc=Definition 1.6.}}</ref>

Note some authors such as nlab require each factorization to be unique.<ref>{{cite web |website=nLab |url=https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/Reedy+category |title=Reedy category}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=The definition of Reedy category |website=mathoverflow |url=https://mathoverflow.net/questions/176983/the-definition-of-reedy-category}}</ref>

== Reedy model structure ==
A Reedy model structure is a canonical model-category structure placed on the functor category M^R when R is a Reedy category and M is a model category.{{expand section|date=April 2025}}

== Eilenberg–Zilber category ==
An '''Eilenberg–Zilber category''' is a variant of a Reedy category.
